namespace: Orchestrate independent background subagents for concurrent collaboration.
instructions: Background collaborators are independent sessions; coordinate them through these tools.

create.description: Start one batch of background collaborators, non-blocking. Every member receives the shared context; a batch with more than one member also receives the launch roster of names, goals and logical addresses. Returns the batch address and member IDs, addresses and names.
create.snippet: Start background collaborators with a shared context
create.guideline:
Write goals in English. subagent_create is non-blocking: after dispatching, continue non-dependent local work or conclude your turn; the creator is woken by internal status, not by polling.

Use a batch when work splits into independent parts that can advance concurrently. Keep tightly coupled sequential steps local, or isolate overlapping file edits in separate git worktrees for you to merge.

Fresh vs Inherited

inheritContext: false (default) starts a member with a clean context. Give it a self-contained goal: background, constraints, scope, deliverable and how to verify completion.

inheritContext: true shares this session's context and capabilities. Use it only when multiple goals (such as separate features) are explicitly required to advance concurrently on top of this session's context. Delegate the part's goal, boundaries and the choices to report back; do not repeat context the member already holds.

Handoff

Members report to the creator with msg_write. The host does not deliver a member's final assistant message as a result. You remain responsible for the final results: verify, integrate, and deliver the overall outcome rather than treating dispatch as completion.

parameters.context: Shared background, constraints and source material every member needs.

agents.description: Batch members in roster order. The roster is fixed at launch.

items.name: Optional caller-facing label used in the roster.
items.goal: This member's part of the work: scope, deliverable and how to verify it.
items.inheritContext: Inherit this session's conversation and capabilities. Default false: start with clean context.

create.capacity: Per-parent caps: at most {batches} active batches, {subagents} active subagents and {inherited} active inherited subagents. A batch or revival that would exceed a cap is refused; running members are not stopped when a cap changes.

list.description: Returns a scoped tree of agents (creator, peers and direct children; capped at 4 per group, active first). Nodes carry IDs, logical addresses, names, one lifecycle status string, roles, kinds and available history paths. Idle nodes are folded.
list.snippet: Read agent names, addresses, statuses and history paths

parameters.all: Show every agent without group limits or folding. Default false.
parameters.id: Filter to a specific agent's visible subtree. Returns null if absent.

list.guideline: Use subagent_list to read agent names, logical addresses, statuses and history file paths.

signal.description: Signal one agent or one agent group by its logical address. interrupt cancels its current tool and model turn but keeps its goal and running Job; stop ends its current Job and releases resources while keeping the Agent and its history.
signal.snippet: Interrupt or stop an agent's current work

parameters.action: interrupt cancels the current tool and model turn and keeps the goal; stop ends the current Job and releases resources.

signal.guideline: Use subagent_signal to interrupt or stop agents; subagent_list shows what each one is doing.

msg_write.description: Send a plain-text message to one logical Agent address. The host binds the sender and the transport framing. A target that is another live session's Main reaches that session's Main; that session sees your session identity and a reply address.
msg_write.snippet: Send plain-text messages to agents through their logical addresses
guidelines: Address one agent by its logical address <sessionHex>:sub_<batch>[-<member>] or <sessionHex>:main from subagent_create, subagent_list or your context.

Broadcast to one batch with <sessionHex>:batch_<batch>, or to one agent's direct children with <sessionHex>:<agent>/children; broadcasts exclude the sender, and addressing yourself directly is rejected.
Messaging a stopped agent revives it for a new round.
A message from another session carries its full session identity and one managed reply address; report back to that reply address with msg_write instead of only outputting in your own turn.
Provide the target address and the message body only; do not add transport envelopes, JSON/NDJSON framing, or a trailing newline.
Keep messages concise; include only key points and necessary context.

parameters.to: One logical Agent address: <sessionHex>:main, <sessionHex>:sub_<batch>[-<member>], <sessionHex>:batch_<batch>, or <sessionHex>:<agent>/children. Never a socket path.
parameters.content: Plain-text message body. The host frames the transport and binds the sender.
